findings.reason: the plan should call these existing struct-level readers on the raw store's IDS objects (they carry no adapter transform) or state why they cannot serve, rather than fork a parallel extractor that will drift from the owner.
findings.text: §1's single reader ("one reader turns a phase's store into drawable families (coil elements, vessel filaments, wall outline, flux loops, probes)", plan lines 108–111) re-implements `read_artifact_pf_active` (line 302), `read_artifact_pf_passive` (line 409), `read_artifact_magnetics` (line 577) and `read_artifact_limiter` (line 671), which already take raw `pf_active` / `pf_passive` / `magnetics` / `wall` IDS structs and return `PFFilament` + `PolygonSection`, `PassiveStructure`, `BProbe` + `FluxLoop`, and a limiter R/Z contour — the exact drawable families the plan wants; the plan cites only the higher `gs` facade (`MachineGeometryService.operator()`, `build_geometry_fields_from_table`), which sits behind the artifact cache, and never names these struct-level readers, so a second, drifting extractor is proposed for behaviour that already exists and is directly callable on the `DBEntry` store.

findings.reason: the plan must reuse the struct-level extractors (or state why a fresh layer is needed); the stated reason for bypassing the adapter does not apply to them.
findings.text: §1 justifies reading the store directly with `imas.DBEntry` instead of `description_reader.read_geometry_table` on the ground that "that route hands back the geometry adapter's table, transformed before the figure would see it", but the reader it then adds is a thin layer whose real subject — element→vertices, probe/loop positions, limiter contour — is already provided by `artifact_*` extractors that are pure functions of the IDS struct and pass through no adapter transform; the justification therefore does not reach the machinery being duplicated.

findings.reason: the section must account for the added interface surface in its own text, as §1 already does for `plot_style.py`.
findings.text: §1b adds a `--palette-candidates` command-line option to `scripts/figures_jt60sa_geometry.py` (and a further eight-candidate surface) without naming what it retires or merges, or stating why nothing can be, while §1 does account for its surface ("it is the first and retires nothing").

duplicate_owner-1.reason: plan v13 §1 has the reader pass the DBEntry IDS to read_artifact_pf_active/pf_passive/magnetics/limiter and draw what they return; §1b moves the landed reader onto them and retires its own element dispatch

interface_budget-1.reason: plan v13 §1b states it widens the table behind the existing --palette-candidates option and adds no option, module or public name

thin_wrapper-1.reason: plan v13 §1 states the artifact_geometry struct-level readers carry no adapter transform and reuses them; the DBEntry read is kept only to open the store

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §1's `imas_ambix/plot_style.py` (named colour roles, the sheet-apply function and the shared direct-label helper) and the geometry script's single reader, reused by §1 and §2 ("calls the same reader rather than reading the store a second time"), hide store traversal behind a surface smaller than what they hide.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan's store→drawable-families reader duplicates the element readers owned by `imas_ambix/gs/artifact_geometry.py` (`read_artifact_pf_active`, `read_artifact_pf_passive`, `read_artifact_magnetics`, `read_artifact_limiter`) rather than extending or calling them.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §1b adds a `--palette-candidates` CLI option without naming what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan states and rests on a 2026-10-06 search of `imas_ambix/data/`, `imas_ambix/gs/` and `scripts/`, naming `paths.py`, `eddb.py`, the machine-map catalogue (`load_packaged_machine_map`, `description_store_root_path`), the `gs` facade and `scripts/validate_mast_geometry.py`; it is a searched plan, though the search missed `gs/artifact_geometry.py` (carried by `duplicate_owner` below).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — the reader §1 adds to `scripts/figures_jt60sa_geometry.py` is a thin re-derivation of element geometry that `imas_ambix/gs/artifact_geometry.py` already extracts from the same raw IDS structs; the plan's stated reason for not extending the existing route does not reach that machinery.
